items.lesson_concept: A Data Subject is an individual whose personal, sensitive personal, or privileged information is processed.
items.question_text: Under the Data Privacy Act, what is the formal term for the individual whose personal information is being collected and processed?
items.explanation: The law formally refers to the living individual whose data is being processed as the 'Data Subject'.

items.lesson_concept: Personal Information is any data, whether recorded in a material form or not, from which the identity of an individual is apparent or can be reasonably and directly ascertained.
items.question_text: Which of the following phrases best defines 'Personal Information' under the DPA?
options: Data from which the identity of an individual is apparent or can be reasonably ascertained.
Data that is permanently kept secret by the government.
Only data that includes a person's medical history.
items.correct_answer: Data from which the identity of an individual is apparent or can be reasonably ascertained.
items.explanation: Section 3(g) defines Personal Information as any information that identifies or can reasonably identify an individual.

items.lesson_concept: Standard Personal Information includes basic identifiers that do not fall into the strict 'sensitive' category, such as a full name, home address, or personal phone number.
items.question_text: Which of the following is an example of standard Personal Information?
items.explanation: A full name is standard Personal Information, while genetics, religion, and blood type are classified as Sensitive Personal Information.

items.lesson_concept: Sensitive Personal Information (SPI) is a special category of personal data subject to much stricter processing rules and higher penalties for mishandling.
items.question_text: What type of personal data is subject to stricter processing rules and higher penalties under the DPA?
items.explanation: SPI requires higher levels of protection and stricter lawful bases for processing compared to standard Personal Information.

items.lesson_concept: Under Section 3(l) of the DPA, any information about an individual's health, medical history, or genetic data is strictly classified as Sensitive Personal Information.
items.question_text: Under the DPA, how is a person's medical diagnosis or health record classified?
items.explanation: Health and medical records are explicitly categorized as Sensitive Personal Information.

items.lesson_concept: Numbers or licenses issued by government agencies peculiar to an individual (such as SSS, GSIS, TIN, or Passport numbers) are classified as Sensitive Personal Information.
items.question_text: Which of the following data points is explicitly considered Sensitive Personal Information (SPI)?
items.explanation: Government-issued identification numbers unique to an individual are classified as SPI.

items.lesson_concept: Privileged Information refers to any data that constitutes privileged communication under the Rules of Court, such as attorney-client or doctor-patient communications.
items.question_text: What classification is given to data protected by legal privilege under the Rules of Court, such as attorney-client communications?
items.explanation: Section 3(k) defines data protected by the Rules of Court as Privileged Information.

items.lesson_concept: A Personal Information Controller (PIC) is a person or organization that controls the collection, holding, processing, or use of personal information.
items.question_text: What do you call the entity that controls the collection, holding, and processing of personal data, essentially deciding the 'why' and 'how'?
items.explanation: The PIC is the ultimate decision-maker regarding the purpose and means of data processing.

items.lesson_concept: A Personal Information Processor (PIP) is any natural or juridical person to whom a PIC outsources the processing of personal data.
items.question_text: What term describes an outsourced third party that processes personal data strictly on behalf of and according to the instructions of another company?
items.explanation: A PIP is an entity that processes data strictly on the documented instructions of a PIC.

items.lesson_concept: A Personal Information Processor (PIP) does not own the data it processes. It acts exclusively upon the documented instructions of the Personal Information Controller (PIC).
items.question_text: Which entity is legally required to act ONLY on the documented instructions of the other?
options: The PIC must act only on the instructions of the PIP.
The PIP must act only on the documented instructions of the PIC.
The Data Subject must act only on the instructions of the DPO.
The DPO must act only on the instructions of the PIP.
items.correct_answer: The PIP must act only on the documented instructions of the PIC.
items.explanation: A PIP has no authority to determine its own purposes for the data; it strictly follows the PIC's instructions.

items.lesson_concept: Processing refers to ANY operation performed on personal data, including collection, recording, organization, storage, updating, retrieval, use, or destruction.
items.question_text: Under the DPA, the term 'Processing' covers which of the following activities?
options: Any operation performed on personal data, from collection to destruction.
items.correct_answer: Any operation performed on personal data, from collection to destruction.
items.explanation: Processing is a comprehensive term that covers the entire lifecycle of data manipulation.

items.lesson_concept: Because 'Processing' includes the destruction of data, companies must follow strict privacy rules even when they are simply deleting or shredding old files.
items.question_text: Is the act of deleting or shredding old personal records considered 'Processing' under the DPA?
options: Yes, destruction and erasure are explicitly defined as forms of processing.
No, processing only refers to active use of data.
No, destroying data removes it from DPA jurisdiction.
Yes, but only for digital files, not paper.
items.correct_answer: Yes, destruction and erasure are explicitly defined as forms of processing.
items.explanation: Section 3(j) explicitly lists erasure and destruction as operations constituting 'processing'.

items.lesson_concept: DPO stands for Data Protection Officer, the individual designated to oversee an organization's compliance with the DPA.
items.question_text: In the context of the Data Privacy Act, what does 'DPO' stand for?
items.explanation: DPO stands for Data Protection Officer, the mandatory compliance champion for PICs and PIPs.

items.lesson_concept: Every Personal Information Controller (PIC) and Personal Information Processor (PIP) is legally mandated to appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO).
items.question_text: Who is required by the DPA to designate a Data Protection Officer (DPO)?
options: Only companies with more than 1,000 employees
Every Personal Information Controller (PIC) and Personal Information Processor (PIP)
items.correct_answer: Every Personal Information Controller (PIC) and Personal Information Processor (PIP)
items.explanation: NPC Circular 16-01 mandates that all PICs and PIPs must appoint an accountable DPO.

items.lesson_concept: Under Section 3(l) of the DPA, an individual's specific age is explicitly classified as Sensitive Personal Information.
items.question_text: According to the strict definitions of the DPA, how is a person's exact age classified?
items.explanation: Section 3(l) explicitly lists age alongside race and marital status as Sensitive Personal Information.

items.lesson_concept: Under Section 3(l) of the DPA, an individual's educational background and records are classified as Sensitive Personal Information.
items.question_text: How does the Data Privacy Act classify information regarding an individual's education or schooling?
items.explanation: Information about an individual's education is explicitly classified as SPI under the law.

items.lesson_concept: Under Section 3(l) of the DPA, information relating to any proceeding for any offense committed or alleged to have been committed by an individual is Sensitive Personal Information.
items.question_text: Is information about an individual's alleged criminal offenses or court proceedings considered Sensitive Personal Information?
options: Yes, it is explicitly classified as Sensitive Personal Information (SPI).
No, it is strictly General Personal Information.
No, it is Public Domain Information exempt from the DPA.
Yes, but only if the individual is convicted.
items.correct_answer: Yes, it is explicitly classified as Sensitive Personal Information (SPI).
items.explanation: Records of offenses committed or alleged are categorized as SPI under the DPA.

items.lesson_concept: Data that has been fully anonymized—meaning it can no longer identify an individual under any circumstances—is no longer considered Personal Information.
items.question_text: If a dataset is fully and permanently anonymized so that no individual can ever be identified from it, is it still considered 'Personal Information'?
options: Yes, all data remains Personal Information forever.
No, fully anonymized data that cannot identify a person is not Personal Information.
Yes, but it is downgraded to Public Information.
No, but the company must still pay a tax on it.
items.correct_answer: No, fully anonymized data that cannot identify a person is not Personal Information.
items.explanation: Personal Information requires that an individual's identity is apparent or ascertainable. True anonymization removes this link.

items.lesson_concept: Personal Information is covered by the DPA whether it is recorded in a material form (like paper or hard drives) or not.
items.question_text: Does 'Personal Information' only refer to data that is permanently saved on a hard drive or written on paper?
options: Yes, unrecorded spoken words can never be regulated.
No, the DPA covers personal information whether recorded in a material form or not.
Yes, it must be stored for at least 24 hours to be considered data.
No, it only refers to encrypted digital data.
items.correct_answer: No, the DPA covers personal information whether recorded in a material form or not.
items.explanation: The definition of Personal Information explicitly states 'whether recorded in a material form or not'.

items.lesson_concept: Under Section 3(l) of the DPA, an individual's marital status is explicitly classified as Sensitive Personal Information.
items.question_text: If a form asks whether a user is 'Single, Married, or Widowed', what classification of data is being collected?
items.explanation: Marital status is expressly listed as Sensitive Personal Information under Section 3(l) of the DPA.
